interpreter.description: How to launch `command` when the operating system cannot do it alone: the program to run followed by any fixed arguments it needs. The adapter's own path is appended after these, then `args`. Omit it on Linux, where a `#!` line and the execute bit are enough. Windows has neither, so a script there must name what runs it, for example ["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-File"].
